chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The free person is not killed for the slave; if the free person kills the slave, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The free person is not killed for the slave, even if he kills him intentionally; rather, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating if he kills him intentionally. And he said: the blood money of the slave is his price.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The slave is killed for the free person, but the free person is not killed for the slave; rather, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating until he recovers.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'Retaliation is prescribed for you in the case of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.' He said: The free person is not killed for the slave, but he receives a severe beating and is liable for his price, the blood money of the slave.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The free person is not killed for the slave; and if the free person kills the slave, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating. And whoever kills him by retaliation or by the fixed punishment, he has no blood money.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no retaliation between the free person and the slave.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he killed a free person for a slave who killed him intentionally, the meaning in this narration is that we interpret it as referring to one who is accustomed to killing slaves, because for such a person it is permissible for the Imam to kill him by it, so that others may be deterred from doing the like. As for if it is unusual and rare from him, then he is not liable for more than his price and discipline, as we have previously mentioned.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

What Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who killed his slave or his female slave, he said: If the slave is his, he is disciplined and detained, unless he is known for killing slaves, in which case he is killed by it.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

From Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who killed his slave, he said: If he is not known for killing, he is given a severe beating and his price is taken from him and paid to the treasury of the Muslims. And if he is accustomed to killing, he is killed by it.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The narrations we mentioned earlier, that the blood money of the slave is his price, are to be understood with the distinction that his price does not exceed the blood money of the free person, because if it exceeds that, it is returned to him, and if it is less, his killer is not liable for more than that.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

What Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The blood money of the slave is his price, and if he is valuable, the best of his price is ten thousand dirhams, and it does not exceed the blood money of the free person.
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If the free person kills the slave, he is liable for his price and is disciplined. It was said: And if his price is twenty thousand dirhams? He said: The price of the slave does not exceed the blood money of the free people.

key_terms.ثَمَن: Price or value, specifically referring to the slave's market value
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation paid to the victim's heirs
key_terms.ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا: A severe beating, a corporal punishment for the killer
key_terms.مُتَعَوِّد: One who is accustomed or habitual

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in compensation when a free person kills a slave versus a slave killing a free person?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling reflects the historical context of slavery where the slave's value was primarily economic, establishing that 'qisas' (equal retaliation) is not strictly applied between a free person and a slave. The primary penalty involves paying the slave's market price as blood money and receiving severe corporal punishment, though the Imam may execute the killer if he is 'accustomed'mu'tad'' (habitual) to ensure deterrence. This distinction highlights the nuanced application of justice in classical Islamic law, balancing economic compensation with punitive measures based on the killer's pattern of behavior.
